title: list --json carries every field lore reads from task view (ODOC-610 / DEC-282 item 1)
description: CARRIER ONLY: filed to own the work; build nothing until a floor-checked brief. ODOC-610 / DEC-282, opum-doc 2026-11-18T23:03Z, from a lore/quest process storm in another fleet (cont1: 2313 tasks, 47 worktrees). lore check and lore sync spawn one quest task view <id> --json per task, about 9 at a time; on 2026-11-12 four to five concurrent runs produced about 45 quest processes and a load of about 128. opum-doc ruling, verbatim for the quest-cli part: "lore-cli, with quest-cli for any field gap: one quest task list --json per run, never a per-task view. Missing fields are added to list JSON (or a multi-id view) by quest-cli. Cache per run keyed by the .quest tree hash. Proof: measured at about 2000 tasks before and after, plus a test that the quest spawn count is bounded regardless of task count." Also ruled verbatim: "quest does not rewrite lore blocks." Items 1-4 ship together in the next lore/quest pair. The exact field gap is named by lore-cli, not guessed here: AC1 is a placeholder until they name it, and the named list belongs on this record.

acceptanceCriteria.text: list --json carries id, aliases, title, status and path for every record, archived ones included under --include-archived, for ids and aliases lore can look up and for a reference that matches more than one record (lore refuses that as ambiguous, it does not rely on list to). Named by lore-cli from src/adapters/quest.ts on origin/dev c28290c2; revision is NOT added to list rows (lore reads it only from task view, for --if-revision)
Measured at about 2000 tasks: list --json returns the same values for the agreed fields as the per-task views it replaces, before and after, reported on this task
A test proves the quest process spawn count is bounded regardless of task count (one spawn per run rather than one per task), with the spawn-count half landing wherever the invoking side lives

A regression test pins that --include-archived rows carry the five fields and that path points into .quest/archive/tasks/ for an archived record, and that a record moved by task complete or archive shows its new path in the very next list call

implementationNotes: lore-cli named the field list 2026-11-21 (src/adapters/quest.ts, origin/dev c28290c2): id, aliases, title, status, path from task list --include-archived --json. No field gap: all five are on list rows (measured by key presence over 575 rows from quest task list --include-archived, 0 rows missing any). revision stays OFF list rows by lore-cli request. Both lore asks confirmed on dev 1cce24f1 in a scratch repo: complete moved path to .quest/completed/T-1.json and archive to .quest/archive/tasks/T-1.json, each visible in the very next list --include-archived call; archived rows in this repo carry id/aliases/title/status/path. Remaining work: AC4 regression test, the ~2000-task measurement (AC2), spawn-count half (AC3, lore side).

#757 landed (squash) at head 097e03c0ac7f7e44f72bb7f80b39e29895003d5d after required checks green on that exact head (source-gates x2, Tracker integrity, lore check) and the review below. Reviewer: Sonnet unit quest-cli-review-757, model claude-sonnet-5-5 verified by argv and transcript, at worktree .claude/worktrees/review-757-097e03c. The reviewer had no shell, so the claims it could not verify (the test passes, the mutation goes red, T-1 is the default id, the 575-row figure) are covered by CI passing on 097e03c0 and by the writer's own red/green proof (mutating path and revision in listFilteredWithPath turned both tests red; restored). Two non-blocking findings are carried to a later quest PR: exit-checks on setup calls plus T-1's archived status asserted in test 1, and the Windows URL pathname. Verdict, verbatim as relayed by team-lead:

VERDICT: APPROVE 097e03c0
The test is real, not mocked, and it covers what the ruling asks for. I found no blocking issues. I read the diff and test/helpers/spawn.ts; I had no shell, so nothing was run.
(1) Real path: APPROVE. quest() runs `bun src/cli/main.ts` through runCommand, which uses Bun.spawnSync. runCommand throws on a signal exit instead of folding it into 0 (QCLI-502). `listed()` runs the real `task list --include-archived --json`, asserts exit 0, and parses `.data`. Nothing is mocked. Dropping a field fails test 1, through the Object.hasOwn loop over FIELDS. A wrong archived path or a stale path after a move fails test 2, through the exact-string equality checks.
(2) Coverage: APPROVE. Test 1 asserts all five fields on every row, archived included. It has a positive control on the id set ["T-1","T-2"], and it asserts `revision` is absent. Test 2 asserts four paths in order: `.quest/tasks/T-1.json` before any move; `.quest/completed/T-1.json` right after complete; `.quest/archive/tasks/T-1.json` right after archive; `.quest/tasks/T-2.json` for the untouched record. Each `row(listed(root), …)` re-reads the list, so each "very next list call" claim is checked directly. Complete and archive are both covered. Both are exit-checked in test 2.
(3) Record consistency: APPROVE. AC4 matches what test 2 proves. The "no revision" assertion goes slightly beyond AC4, but AC1 records the revision decision, so that is fine. All ACs stay unchecked, which is correct: AC2 and AC3 are still open, and AC1 and AC4 can be checked at finalization. The implementation note says "Remaining work" and includes AC4. If it merges as-is, the note should get a follow-up once the test is merged.
(4) Flakiness, leftover state, platform: NON-BLOCKING, test:47-49, 73-75, 88: setup calls (init, create, edit, and in test 1 complete and archive) are not exit-checked. A failed setup surfaces later as a confusing assertion, not at the failing step. Test 1's positive control would still catch a missing T-1 or T-2. It would not catch an archive that silently failed. The row would then be a completed row, and test 1 never asserts status or path, so the "archived included" claim would be weaker than it reads. Suggested fix: assert exitCode 0 on those calls, and assert T-1's status in the listing, or its archive path, in test 1. NON-BLOCKING, test:34: `new URL(...).pathname` yields a bad path on Windows (`/C:/…`). Test 2's literal forward-slash paths would also be wrong if quest emitted backslashes. I could not verify how other tests handle this. Likely it is the same pattern already used elsewhere in the tree, and the repo's CI is hosted Linux and macOS. Leftover state: afterAll removes every tmp root, with force. A throw before `roots.push` is impossible, because mkdtemp returns first. No fixed ports and no shared state. The pre-existing git hook and trunk concerns don't apply to a tmpdir repo. Env leakage: quest() passes no `env`, so it inherits the parent's. Any QUEST_* variable set in the parent could alter behaviour. This is the same risk as other tests and is not new. `git init -q` is awaited. No git identity is needed, because the test makes no commits.
Could not verify without a shell: the writer's claim that mutating the list path turns the test red; whether the test passes at all; whether `task edit --status "In Progress"` then `complete` is the legal transition (per memory, complete refuses To Do→Done, so the edit step is right); whether the id format `T-1` is what `init` yields in a fresh tmp workspace (I saw `"T-1"` used in other tests, but did not confirm the default prefix); the "575 rows" measurement in the record note.
